hebrews.9.p1.b1.text: Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and also an earthly sanctuary.

hebrews.9.p1.b2.text: In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the consecrated bread. This was called the Holy Place.

hebrews.9.p1.b3.text: Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place, containing … the gold-covered ark of the covenant.

hebrews.9.p1.b4.text: But we cannot discuss these things in detail now.

hebrews.9.p2.b5.text: … the priests entered regularly into the first room to perform their sacred duties.

hebrews.9.p2.b6.text: But only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year …

hebrews.9.p2.b7.text: By this arrangement the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing.

hebrews.9.p2.b8.text: … the gifts and sacrifices being offered were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper.

hebrews.9.p3.b9.text: But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come, …

hebrews.9.p3.b10.text: … He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption.

hebrews.9.p3.b11.text: … the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean,

hebrews.9.p3.b12.text: how much more will the blood of Christ … purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!

hebrews.9.p4.b13.text: Therefore Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance …

hebrews.9.p4.b14.text: In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it,

hebrews.9.p4.b15.text: because a will does not take effect until the one who made it has died; it cannot be executed while he is still alive.

hebrews.9.p5.b16.text: That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.

hebrews.9.p5.b17.text: For when Moses … took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people,

hebrews.9.p5.b18.text: “This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep.”

hebrews.9.p5.b19.text: … without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

hebrews.9.p6.b20.text: For Christ did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary, but He entered heaven itself, now to appear on our behalf in the presence of God.

hebrews.9.p6.b21.text: Nor did He enter heaven to offer Himself again and again, as the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.

hebrews.9.p6.b22.text: But now He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself.

hebrews.9.p7.b23.text: Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,

hebrews.9.p7.b24.text: so also Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many;

hebrews.9.p7.b25.text: and He will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.
